findings.trigger: The Tailored entry calls hiltViewModel<TailorViewModel>(key = applicationId) and then hiltViewModel<TailoredViewModel>(key = applicationId) in the same per-entry ViewModelStore. lifecycle 2.10.0 ViewModelProviderImpl.getViewModel finds a TailorViewModel under that key, fails isInstance, creates TailoredViewModel and calls store.put(key, vm), which runs oldViewModel.clear() and cancels TailorViewModel.viewModelScope. The instance handed to TailoredRoute is therefore always cleared, so tapping Undo, Accept changes or Export PDF launches into a cancelled scope and does nothing; Export never enables. No test composes the real entry (TailorEntryKeysTest only resolves the NavEntry; ShellHarness renders placeholders).
findings.title: Two ViewModels share one store key in the Tailored entry; TailorViewModel is cleared, so Undo/Accept/Export are no-ops
findings.proof: Plain JUnit: val store = ViewModelStore(); val p = ViewModelProvider.create(store, factory); val a = p["app-1", TailorViewModel::class]; p["app-1", TailoredViewModel::class]; assertTrue(a.viewModelScope.isActive) fails. Fix: distinct keys (e.g. "tailor-$id"/"tailored-$id") or drop the key (the entry store is already per-key).

findings.rule: 278-c2 exactly one SPEND per tailoring; no double spend on re-entry/process death
findings.trigger: User starts tailoring and backgrounds the app; the run finishes in viewModelScope (SPEND recorded, application upserted) but the Replace to Tailored waits for collectAsStateWithLifecycle to resume. The OS kills the process; rememberNavBackStack restores TailoringNavKey, a new TailoringViewModel runs the runner again unconditionally, records a second SPEND and overwrites the tailored resume (changesAcceptedAt reset). The same happens if the process dies between record() and upsertApplication(), which are two separate writes.
findings.title: Restored Tailoring screen re-runs tailoring and spends a second credit
